info.title: Tools — cat-harness
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Assemble every declared `memory` directory's nodes into each agent's memory, per vendor: Claude Code's `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md` (a marked region, injected when the subagent starts) and Antigravity's workspace skill `.agents/skills/<agent>-memory/SKILL.md`. Other vendors (Gemini CLI, Copilot, Codex, Cursor) are not generated.

memory.description: Each agent's assembled memory file, per vendor.

post.summary: Check that an ArchiMate model's fhir-actor tags point at the IG's FHIR ActorDefinitions
post.description: Actors come first: the IG's ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK's personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property `fhir-actor`, whose value is an ActorDefinition's canonical URL, and the IG's ActorDefinitions: FSH `InstanceOf: ActorDefinition` under `input/fsh/`, and FHIR JSON under `fsh-generated/resources/` or `input/resources/`, each canonical being `<sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id>` unless its `url` says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a `#person` actor on an application or technology element, a `#system` actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; `--strict` makes that a failure. `--json` prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate model is read.

model.description: The model's id from the config.

ig.description: The IG directory holding `sushi-config.yaml` and `input/fsh/`; absent, the layer root.

strict.description: Fail, not only warn, when an ActorDefinition is realized by no element of the model.

json.description: Print the back-links as JSON (element → actors, actor → elements, problems, unrealized) instead of the report.

report.description: The problems, the unrealized ActorDefinitions and a summary line; with `--json`, the back-links as JSON. Exit 1 on any problem, or on an unrealized actor under `--strict`.

x-selection.when: In an IG whose systems are drawn in an ArchiMate model, after its ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK personas: when model authors tag boxes `fhir-actor` in Archi, in CI, and before generating pages that link boxes to actors.
x-selection.limits: Reads one model per run. Checks pointers only: it never creates an ActorDefinition, and an actor missing from the IG is added there, by hand, from its persona. Reads FSH by pattern, not with SUSHI, so an ActorDefinition made only through a RuleSet is not seen until its JSON is generated.
x-selection.cost: One parse of the model and of the IG's FSH; milliseconds. No network, no JVM, no SUSHI.

post.summary: Draw a document's tables and figures from its ArchiMate data, and check the model against the document's relationship rules
post.description: For each table a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` lists under `tables`, rewrites the block's Markdown table from an `archimate-relationship-rules/v1` file (`relationship-rules`: source, relationship, target, note; `relationship-types`: picture, verb, meaning), keeping the caption and footnotes. For each figure under `figures` that names an `svg`, writes the view as SVG (the same drawing as the view's page). For a rules table that names a `model`, reports the rules the model never uses, the relationships no rule covers, the rules ArchiMate's relationship table refuses, and the relationship types the rules use without a meaning. The rules are in charge: nothing is rewritten from the model.

instance.description: The layer root whose config, models, rules and blocks are read.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a block or SVG is not what the data draws.

strict.description: Also exit 1 when the model has relationships no rule covers, or a rule is one ArchiMate does not allow.

blocks.description: The rewritten table blocks and figure SVGs, at the paths the config names; the rules check on stdout.

x-selection.when: When a document's table or figure restates an ArchiMate model (the element and relationship types it uses, the rules between them, a view): generate it instead of typing it, and run `--check` in CI so it cannot drift.
x-selection.limits: Draws relationship tables and view figures only; element-type tables and glossary tables are not covered yet. Checks a relationship's end types only, not derivation chains or viewpoints.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model named, one table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Check a layer's ArchiMate models against its config
post.description: The ArchiMate gate (graph typology `archimate`): every model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names is held, parses (Archi's native XML or its zipped archive), and resolves — every box in every view draws an element the model holds, every relationship's ends are in the model — and no `.archimate` file is held that the config does not name.

instance.description: The layer root whose `archimate` directory is checked.

problems.description: One line per problem on stderr, exit 1; or one ✓ line, exit 0.

x-selection.when: Before publishing a layer's ArchiMate models, and in its CI: a model that will not parse, draws an element it does not hold, or is held without being configured.
x-selection.limits: Archi's native format only; the Open Group exchange format is not read yet.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Count the tangles in ArchiMate views: lines crossing lines, and lines through boxes
post.description: For each view, as `render-view.ts` draws it, count the pairs of lines that cross and the lines that run through a box they do not connect (groups, and boxes that hold one of the line's ends, excepted). With `--view` it lists each tangle by the boxes it joins; with `--max` it is a gate.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

max.description: Exit 1 if any view has more tangles than this.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

tangles.description: Per view: crossings and lines through a box.

x-selection.when: Before and after every change to an ArchiMate view, so a change never adds tangles (skill `archimate-models`, "Untangle every view you touch").
x-selection.limits: Counts the lines as drawn by this harness's renderer, which draws a stale Archi route straight; Archi itself may draw the same view slightly differently.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
post.description: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without `--apply` it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes' bounds and the re-routed lines' bendpoints changing.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

routes-only.description: Never move a box; only re-route lines.

apply.description: Write the model back in place.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

report.description: Per view: tangles before and after, and the swaps and routes made.

x-selection.when: After drawing or changing an ArchiMate view, before committing it: run it, look at the drawing, keep what reads better (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.limits: A greedy search, one line or one swap at a time: it lowers tangles but does not find the best layout, never adds, resizes or regroups boxes, and leaves lines that end on lines, or share both ends with another line, as they are. The author still looks at the result.
x-selection.cost: Seconds for a large view (about 8 s for 20 views). No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Derive the metamodel an ArchiMate model uses, and check it against ArchiMate's relationship table
post.description: For each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names: the element types it uses, with counts; every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern its relationships follow, with counts and ids; whether ArchiMate's relationship table (Appendix B of ArchiMate 3.2, as Archi holds it, committed as `archimate/schemas/archimate-relationships.json` in the tools layer) allows each pattern; and the placeholder elements, named after their own type, that a hand-drawn metamodel leaves in a model. Prints a report, JSON, Graphviz DOT or a Mermaid class diagram. `archimate-pages` draws the same result on each model's "Metamodel in use" page, so the metamodel is derived, never drawn.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate models are read.

model.description: One model's id from the config; absent, every model. Required for `--format dot` and `mmd`.

check.description: Exit 1 when any relationship follows a pattern ArchiMate does not allow. Placeholders are reported, never fatal.

metamodel.description: The report, or the metamodel as `archimate-metamodel/v1` JSON, DOT or Mermaid, on stdout.

x-selection.when: Before publishing an ArchiMate model (process `archimate-publish`, after `archimate-check`), in its CI, and whenever someone asks which element types and relationships a model actually uses — instead of drawing a metamodel view by hand.
x-selection.limits: Checks each relationship's type against its ends' types only; it does not check derivation chains, viewpoints or properties. A type the table does not know is reported as not checked, never as refused.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model and a table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Give every ArchiMate view, element and relationship a page and an IRI, and draw every view
post.description: Write a JSON-LD node and a thin page for each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names and for every view, element and relationship in it — keyed by Archi's own ids — plus the normalised model the pages' one loader draws from, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own bounds and bendpoints in ArchiMate's notation, each box a link to its element. `--out` writes into a site being built — the data at the graph's path, the pages at the route of the visualiser the layer declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`; without it the files go into the graph and `--check` gates them.

out.description: A site being built: the data lands at `<out>/<graph path>/` and the pages at `<out>/<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`, the route of the layer's one visualiser `renderedBy` this Tool (none declared: nothing is written). Absent, they are written into the graph, which must be `served: true`.

check.description: Without `--out`: fail if a committed page is missing, stale or orphaned; write nothing.

pages.description: Pages and view drawings written (or found current).

x-selection.when: A folio's staging or publish build should show its ArchiMate models: run after the document site is built and before the navbar pass.
x-selection.limits: Draws the notation, not Archi's icons, custom images or fonts; sketch and canvas views are skipped. Never replaced by Archi's CLI report (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view; four models of 5,809 pages and 131 drawings (~24 MB) take about 1.5 s. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Check a bean is free, then claim it on every copy
post.description: For one bean: fetch every bean copy, read the last three commits on its file, skip it if another agent committed within the window or its last note is a claim, look for an open PR naming it in every listed repository, and only then set it in-progress with a dated claim note as a plain commit on every copy. A rejected push is fetched, rebased and re-checked, never forced.

id.description: The bean, full or short id.

copy.description: A local checkout of a bean copy. Repeat once per copy. Defaults to the current checkout.

repo.description: A repository whose open PRs are searched for the id. Repeat. Defaults to the copies' repositories.

minePr.description: The link of an open PR that is the caller's own, when resuming a bean it already holds. Every cloud thread's PR has the same author, so without this any open PR naming the bean is a skip.

as.description: Which agent is asking, by its name in the agents table. Defaults to `cloud`.

session.description: The caller's session link, matched against the `Claude-Session:` trailer so a sibling thread of the same agent is told apart. Defaults to $CLAUDE_SESSION_URL.

agents.description: A JSON file of agents and their commit authors, as in the skill's input schema.

dryRun.description: Check only; report `would-claim` and write nothing.

json.description: Emit `definitions.claimCheck` as JSON.

check.description: One of claimed, would-claim, skip-recent-commit, skip-claim-note, skip-open-pr, skip-closed or unknown, with the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Exit 0 for claimed or would-claim, 1 for a skip, 2 for unknown. Unknown is never reported as free. With --json, `definitions.claimCheck` of schemas/skills/bean-drain/output.schema.json.

result.description: With --json, the check as one `BeanClaimCheck` record: the state, the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Programs and BPMN gateways read this; people read `check`.

x-selection.when: Before any work on a bean, when more than one agent may be draining the same store.
x-selection.limits: It sees commits and open PRs, not an agent's intent: an agent that works without committing or opening a PR is invisible until it does. One bean per call. `beans:claim` is the right claim when the store has one copy and no other agents drain it.
x-selection.cost: One fetch and one push per copy, and one paged GitHub REST listing of open PRs per repository.

format.description: Output format: table, json, or ids.

report.description: Query results formatted as a table, JSON or IDs, for people to read.

result.description: The rows as one `BeanQueryRows` record, each variable to its value with bean IRIs shortened to ids: `structuredContent.rows` over MCP in every format, and the text itself with format json. Programs and BPMN gateways read this; people read `report`.

post.description: Read and write the work plan with the `beans` binary. The normal mechanism when it is installed.

id.description: The bean to act on; absent for list/create.

x-selection.when: The normal case, once `scripts/install-beans.sh` has run. It is the only arm that can answer what an item IS or what it waits on — the fallback gives titles and statuses and nothing else — so any work that involves choosing, claiming or reasoning about an item wants this one.
x-selection.limits: Absent on a fresh container until installed, and the install can fail. It is third-party, which is why `.beans.yml` is one of the two configuration paths `check:harness-dirs` cannot remove. When it is missing, `beans-manual` writes the same store in the same layout and this reads back everything it wrote.
x-selection.cost: One install step per container, and it wants network to fetch. Nothing at runtime after that.

post.description: Read and write the same work plan without the CLI — `scripts/beans-fallback.ts`, or editing a bean's front matter directly. Equal standing to the CLI, not a degraded mode.

x-selection.when: When the CLI is not installed and cannot be — not a rare case: a fresh container has no `beans` on PATH. Equal standing, not a degraded mode. An agent that knows only the CLI reads the plan and touches nothing, which is exactly the 2026-09-18 session that completed two merged PRs' worth of durable work UNCLAIMED.
x-selection.limits: Titles and statuses only. It cannot say what an item is, what it depends on, or what it waits on — enough to CLAIM and to record, not enough to CHOOSE. Install `beans-cli` when the choice is the point.
x-selection.cost: None. The store is files in the repository, so this needs a filesystem and nothing else — which is also why it is the arm that survives an air-gapped or sovereign-compute layer.

post.description: Generate, per diagram, a checklist that walks the BPMN as a state machine: each task names the `workflow_complete` call that records it and ends with `next:` by node id; each decision lists its labelled branches (or the DMN that computes it); parallel forks name every branch and joins wait for all; start/end events are entry and exit lines. A rendering, never an authority: it says it is generated, and `--check` fails when one is stale.

out.description: Write every `<stem>.checklist.md` into this one directory instead. Default: each beside its diagram, in the layer that owns it; the harness site's `assets/workflows/checklists` holds those of the layers below the harness.

check.description: Verify instead of write: exit 1 on a stale, missing or orphaned checklist.

checklists.description: One committed `<stem>.checklist.md` per diagram in every layer, beside its `.bpmn`.

x-selection.when: A coding agent needs a process in a form it can follow without reading BPMN XML, or without the engine's MCP server.
x-selection.limits: Conditions are the flows' labels or the DMN's id; a condition expression the model does not carry is not reproduced. The engine stays the authority.
x-selection.cost: One diagram load per process; no network.

post.summary: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer's own site, or a branches/<branch> preview
post.description: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer's own gates (`--pre`), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (`/<repo>`, or `/<repo>/branches/<branch>` for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. It never decides to publish: only `--publish` does, and then a root publish keeps `branches/` and `_render-log/` on the branch, and a preview replaces only its own `branches/<branch>/`.

root.description: The layer checkout (holds `index.config.json`). Default: the working directory.

instance.description: The declared layer name; must match the checkout's declaration.

home.description: A page that becomes the site's index.md.

pre.description: A package script to run in the checkout first, as `bun run <name>` (repeatable): the layer's own gates. Any non-zero exit stops the build.

sourceStep.description: A package script that writes into the site source, run as `bun run <name> <site source>` (repeatable).

siteStep.description: A package script that writes finished pages into the BUILT site, run as `bun run <name> <built site>` after Jekyll (repeatable): Jekyll drops `_`-prefixed directories, so a generator whose pages sit under one runs here.

staging.description: Build (and with --publish, publish) a preview of this branch at branches/<branch>/.

noMount.description: Use the mounts already on disk.

publish.description: Publish after every check passes; needs --remote.

remote.description: The https git URL the caller can push the pages branch to.

site.description: The built site directory, and its base path.

links.description: Pages checked, unresolved links (must be 0), files.

x-selection.when: Publishing a layer's site, or a branch preview of it, from an agent or a Routine: the agent-run replacement for a pages workflow.
x-selection.limits: Layer sites only. A FHIR IG's site (the IG pipeline layer's `stage-ig-sites`) is not built here yet; it needs the IG's FHIR packages, which some environments cannot reach.
x-selection.cost: A full mount, install and Jekyll build: minutes, not seconds. `--no-mount` reuses what is on disk.

post.summary: Do the Tool nodes agree with their skills?
post.description: Check every Tool node's joins: that each `satisfies` resolves to a real skill and agrees with that skill's declared contract, that every io port names a declared type, and that no argv input has a type able to express a shell payload.

report.description: The satisfies map, the count of skills with and without a Tool, then the verdict. Exit 0 every join holds, 1 at least one does not. A skill with NO Tool is reported and is NOT a failure: many skills are pure judgement, and failing on them would make the report unusable.

x-selection.when: Before pushing any change to `tools/`, and as the first of the three audits `code-node-review` lists. It is the check that refuses a contract nobody could satisfy.
x-selection.limits: It checks the JOINS, not the truth: a node can pass while its `invoke` names a command that does something else entirely. That is a reviewer's to catch, which is why the skill exists and not a check script alone.
x-selection.cost: Seconds. Loads the Tool graph and the skill corpus in-process.

post.summary: Is CI passing on the default branch?
post.description: Report each workflow's state on the default branch, which a checkout cannot see: a red workflow looks exactly like a green one from in here. One API call over the recent run history, not one request per workflow, so it stays inside the unauthenticated 60/hr limit and stays usable at session start.

markdown.description: Emit the block the session-start sweep prints. ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as `if ! …; then`, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red.

warn.description: Report only, never fail. For a caller that wants the state without a verdict.

out.description: Write the markdown report to a file AND keep the exit code — which `--markdown` cannot do, since it always exits 0. Its own flag, so one API call is not spent twice.

report.description: One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, `running`, `superseded` (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or `--out` could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. `--markdown` and `--warn` always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither.

x-selection.when: Before trusting ANY workflow's outcome, and at session start: a workflow's result is invisible from a checkout.
x-selection.limits: It reads the DEFAULT BRANCH, so on a PR it describes `main` and not the diff — which is why it is deliberately not one of the `gates`. `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` is used when present; without one a public repo still works and a private one fails. A REFUSED OR FAILING API CALL EXITS 2 AND IS NEVER GREEN: could-not-look must stay distinguishable from looked-and-it-was-fine.
x-selection.cost: One HTTP request; fast enough for the session-start sweep, which is why it makes a single call.

post.summary: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
post.description: Before a model reads a sub-agent's report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are `control` (steers what the receiver does) or `data` (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator's plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. Exit 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 quarantined, 2 could not determine.

With `--write` it moves `remoteMounts` off the declaration into `source.remote` entries, writes the generated `.gitignore` block, and renames a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` to `index.lock.json`. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. post.summary: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
post.description: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness's declaration at its pin and every `needs`, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless --repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch's tip unless --pin says otherwise, its declaration's name checked), seeds them all into the repository's index.config.json with the consent given (`remote-mount --seed --whole`), sets `site.landing` to the harness, `site.agentRun` and `mountApprovers`, mounts the closure (`remote-mount`: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (`.github/cat.ts` and `.github/mount-from-lock.sh` from cat-harness-tools `templates/root-bootstrap/`) and sets the root's `cat` script to `bun .github/cat.ts`, so `bun run cat …` mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness's `instantiate:<harness>` checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/<harness>). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:<harness>` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches/<branch>/ (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin <name>=<sha>` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of <name>=<owner/repo>` says where a need lives.

harness.description: The harness, OWNER/REPO, pinned at its default branch's tip (pin it otherwise with --pin <name>=<sha>).

Re-pinning an already harnessed repository is remote-mount --seed, not this.
x-selection.cost: The mount: a blobless fetch of each layer of the closure and one install (a few minutes). Then the harness's prepare step (an IG's AST: a full IG Publisher run) and the render.

post.description: Read every `user-scenario` and `workshop` node in the checkout through the layers' declared directories, with the journeys viewer's own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (`personas`, a step's `lead`, `experiences[].actor`, `handoff.from`/`to`, `illustrationStyle.cast[].actor`), user stories, `realisedBy` BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, `uses` blocks in a directory declaring `building-blocks`, `req:` requirements, FHIR examples and a step's `dak` assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a `fhir-artifact-index` (could not determine while the index is built at publish), `illustration.src` files, `follows`/`partOf`/`parts`/`includes` journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an `includes` held against the call activity its step's `realisedBy` names, could not determine when the call names no process), the `trustLadder` code list and each `record.state` code of it, and ArchiMate `views`; and each workshop's `scenarios`, `steps[]` `{scenario, step}` and `<scenario>#<step>` refs; each device screen's `owner` and `personCard` actors, its `steps[]` `{scenario, step}`, and the FHIR examples its `qr` and `recordList` blocks name; and every persona's `avatar` image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind `specialises` it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part's `follows` or `partOf`, personas equal to the parts', a lead equal to the lanes' first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. With a token it publishes the verdict as the commit status `judge-tree`; `check` answers whether any runner judged a digest green; `sample` re-runs a seeded few gates of a record.

test-path.description: What `bun test` runs on each side; none means no tests.

publish.description: Post the commit status `judge-tree` when GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN is set; without one, the record file is the verdict.

record.description: The verdict record, `<records-dir>/<treeDigest>.json` unless --out names it; valid against the tools layer's `schemas/verdict-record.schema.json`. Three exit codes: 0 green, 1 red, 2 COULD NOT DETERMINE (no judging scripts, a stored base verdict for another tree, a compare script that crashed, or no gate ran). 2 is never green, and neither is a verdict for another digest.

x-selection.cost: That of layer-pr-checks for one side, or two when no stored base verdict exists: gates dominate (minutes to tens of minutes). `digest` and `check` are one hash and at most one HTTP request.

post.summary: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
post.description: Lay down each declared remote mount — a `source.remote` layer in the root `index.config.json`, or, in a folio with no index, a `remoteMounts` entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, `index.lock.json` (a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root `.gitignore` block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through `writeDeclaredMounts` into `index.config.json`. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (`schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts`, rule H8): a person's consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. `--staging` mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or `mountDefaults` names may be one the layer declares in its `<name>.json` or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (`skills/skills.json` naming `voices`), resolved at the pin through `instanceDirectories`; an id in neither is refused at plan time. `tools` on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (`<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts`), its implementation (the `inProcess.module`, or the script its `bun run cat <key>` resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools' `importClosure` (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A `hydrated` mount lays each chosen directory down as its published `index.hydrated.jsonld` only: read from the pin's git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin's subgraph index package (the `subgraph-index-<sha>` release asset `subgraph-index-package` publishes), its tarball checked against its `folio-binary-release/v1` record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, `SubgraphHydratedSchema` and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package's URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. `--check` compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (`skill:commands` → `.claude/commands/`, `agent-memory` → `.claude/agent-memory/` and `.agents/`) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and `--no-agent-surface` opts out.

instance.description: The downstream layer root; omitted, every declaring layer in the checkout.

staging.description: Mount for a staging preview: no signature or consent required.

check.description: Compare the disk against the lock; fetch nothing.

noAgentSurface.description: Do not re-render `.claude/commands/` and the agent memory after a mount that changed the lock.

noInstall.description: Lay the pinned bytes down without `bun install` in each mounted layer that carries a `package.json`. By default the install runs (`--production`; `--install-all` keeps devDependencies), so the mounted tools run; it writes only `node_modules/`, which no mount digest covers, so `--check` still passes.

seed.description: `<name>=<owner/repo>@<40-char sha>`: create or re-pin that remote layer in `index.config.json` instead of mounting, writing its `trust.consent` for that pin in the same write (needs `consentBy` and `evidence`; repeatable; `--whole` mounts every tracked file). Refused while a mount it moves has edits the lock does not hold, since the next mount would leave that mount at the old commit; `fresh` lets it through.

fresh.description: Replace a mount whose bytes no longer hash to the lock instead of leaving it untouched; with `seed`, re-pin over such edits. The edits are discarded.

choose.description: `<harness>[:<instance>]`: write a review's choice (`directories` and/or `tools`) into that mount entry's `overrides.<instance>` instead of mounting, so a fresh clone replays it. The pin and its consent are untouched; the next mount resolves the choice and the lock records what it resolved to.

directories.description: With `choose`: comma-separated directory ids, nested ids or concern names.

tools.description: With `choose`: comma-separated Tool ids, each mounted runnable.

evidence.description: With `seed`: where the consent was given, readable (a session, an issue comment), as `consent.evidence`. On stdin because it is free prose: it quotes what was said.

outcomes.description: Per layer: mounted, local, skipped, missing (including refused by the trust gate) or could-not-determine.

post.summary: Record what the publish branch served
post.description: Append one entry to the render log on the publish branch: what was published or taken down, when, from which commit, and — for a removal or a retention — WHY. The log is the only place a preview that vanished leaves a trace.

dir.description: A checkout of the publish branch, or a publish directory about to become one. This tool NEVER fetches, commits or pushes: the calling workflows hold the checkout with their own retry and concurrency handling, and a second pusher racing them could lose a deploy.

event.description: `rendered`, `removed`, `restored` or `retained`. `retained` records a removal CONSIDERED and refused, which would otherwise leave no trace.

kind.description: What was rendered — `staging-preview`, `site`, `export`. Open, not an enum: the publish branch carries more than previews, and an enum would make logging a new kind wait on a schema change.

path.description: The path on the publish branch. Checked as a VALUE, never trusted by provenance: the slug sanitiser can emit `..`, which is only safe for a slug taken from a git ref, and a dispatch input is not one.

slug.description: The staging slug, where the subject has one.

branch.description: The branch the render came from.

commit.description: The commit the artefact was built from.

run.description: The workflow run that wrote this, so a reader can open the log.

prose.description: One JSON object on STDIN: `{summary, reason?, detail?, format?}`. `summary` is required and one line. `reason` is required by the SCRIPT for `removed` and `retained`, because an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity the log exists to prevent. `format` declares how the prose reads (absent means plain text, never sniffed). Build it with `jq -n --arg`, never by concatenation.

entry.description: The day's JSONL the entry was APPENDED to. Append is the only verb: there is no `--remove`, no `--edit` and no `--id`, so a takedown is a `removed` ENTRY rather than the erasure of the `rendered` one before it, and the never-delete rule is structural rather than a guard every cleanup path must remember.

x-selection.when: Whenever something is published to or removed from the publish branch — including a removal that was refused. Called from `feature-staging.yml` at four points; `staging-render-log.bpmn` is the process.
x-selection.limits: It writes into a directory and does not push, so a caller that forgets to commit the log has written nothing durable. It cannot edit or delete an entry, by design. `--summary` / `--reason` / `--detail` are REFUSED as flags at exit 2 rather than ignored: they go on stdin, and a caller still passing them is told instead of silently logging an entry with no summary.
x-selection.cost: One appended line. No network.

post.summary: The render pipeline, in dependency order
post.description: Flatten the repository's renders into the order their `needs` imply, and optionally run them. Two stages: the current declared state as json/jsonld and the README derived from it are FATAL; the dynamic renderers (viewers, visualisers, doc pages, diagrams) skip and log; the dynamic-state export closes it. A cycle or a missing dependency yields NO order rather than a partial one.

dry_run.description: Print the flattened order and each step's failure policy without running anything.

report.description: Per step: ran, failed, skipped, or PENDING — declared with no implementation yet, which is never rendered as a pass.

post.summary: Rewrite paths that still name a moved file's old layer — never in a record
post.description: After a move between two layers lands, find every mention `<from>/<prefix>/<rest>` in the scanned tree's tracked files and rewrite it to `<to>/<prefix>/<rest>` only when the file exists under the destination root and not under the source root. Records are never read: beans, todos, memory, proposals, wireframes, QA results, upstream pins, vocab mappings, provenance figures and terminologies, and test fixtures (`DEFAULT_RECORD_GLOBS`; the CLI's `--keep <glob>` adds more, generated trees among them, which their generators rewrite — a glob is not a shell-safe argument type, so it is not a declared input). Reports by default with file and line; `--write` applies; `--check` exits 1 while a rewrite is owed.

toName.description: The layer the files moved to.

scan.description: The git checkout whose tracked files are read; default the source root.

check.description: Exit 1 while any rewrite is owed; write nothing.

rewrites.description: Rewrites made or owed, each with file and line; mentions left alone; record files not read.

schemaReference.description: The generated reference directory. Never hand-edited.

post.description: Find graph nodes, authored or ingested, whose label, title, kind or tags contain a string, with no graph expansion. corpus-search composes this with a neighbour walk.

post.summary: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
post.description: Compare each repository's declared credential needs (`credentials/needs.json`, profile and registry) with the `secrets.NAME` expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions' dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0.

repos.description: Repository checkouts to check. Default: every repository the index mounts.

json.description: Print the result as JSON instead of the human report.

verdict.description: The exit status: 0 clean, 1 a major or critical finding, 2 could not determine.

x-selection.limits: Presence on GitHub is judged only when a token may list secret names (`list-secret-names`); without one that half is could-not-determine, never clean.
x-selection.cost: Reads workflow and declaration files; one API call per repository when a token is present.

post.summary: Run every existing security check as one named release step
post.description: Run the repository's security checks — workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile pinning, the toolchain pin, QA reviewer permission, materialised-asset fixity — plus two advisories (dependency advisories, third-party action SHA pinning), each by name as argv. Every check is reported as pass, fail or unknown; a blocking check that fails OR could not be run refuses the release, because could-not-check is never clean. Advisories are reported and never block. Called by `prepare-merge` before a push that will merge, and by any publish process before it publishes.

json.description: Print a `folio-security-gate/v1` result on stdout instead of the human report.

blocked.description: Whether a blocking check failed or could not be run; also the exit status (1 when blocked).

post.summary: Is this repository's cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
post.description: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: `mounts` (every declared layer on disk at its pin — `remote-mount --check`), `declarations` (every path a declaration names resolves — `declaration-resolution`), `monorepo-paths` (no wiring still names the monorepo: `livesAt` on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), `import-direction` and `reference-direction` (no layer reaches a layer above it), and `site` (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — `build-instance-site --no-mount`, only with `--site`). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without `--site` the answer is never 0.

root.description: The separated checkout. Default: the working directory.

site.description: Build the site from the mounts on disk (minutes); without it the `site` condition is not run and the verdict cannot be complete.

monorepo.description: The repository the separation left, `<owner>/<repo>`. Default: litlfred/folio-assistant.

monorepoDir.description: Its old checkout directory name, as paths spell it. Default: the repository's name.

json.description: Print the report as JSON, mounted-layer findings included.

conditions.description: Per condition: pass, fail, could-not-determine or not-run, the gate that decided it, and its findings.

x-selection.when: Before calling a separation's cutover (kg-separation stage 13) done, and after any re-pin of a separated repository's layers.
x-selection.limits: It judges ONE repository. A downstream's own CI and the parent repository's retirement are not observed from here.
x-selection.cost: Seconds without `--site`; a full Jekyll build with it.

post.description: Write each shared directory of a built site (its `assets/…` laid out as a built site) to `<out>/shared/<dir>/<key>/` with a `.shared.json`, so sites on one host load one copy instead of one each. A directory already there is left alone. This is the host side of the shared-assets step `build-instance-site` runs when a checkout declares `site.sharedAssets`; run on its own, it stages an IG build, or any built site, into a host site root.

out.description: The host site root the shared directories are written under.

staged.description: One line per shared directory: `staged` or `already there`, with its path under `shared/`.

x-selection.when: Composing a layer's site for a host that serves shared assets, or staging an IG build's assets into such a host.
x-selection.limits: Copies only; it does not rewrite the pages that load the assets. `build-instance-site` does both in one run.
x-selection.cost: A local copy of the shared directories: seconds.

post.description: List the Claude Code sessions that have committed to this repository in a time window, from the `Claude-Session:` trailer on commits across ALL branches — with each one's commit count, first and last commit, latest subject, and the branches containing its tip. The session API cannot see a sibling session, so the trailer is the only durable session identity here and a session's state is INFERRED from its branch; whether a session is still running is not knowable from a checkout and is deliberately not reported.

json.description: Emit the sweep as JSON rather than the report.

result.description: With --json, the sweep as one `SessionSweep` record: the sessions, the commits examined and how many carried no trailer. Programs read this; people read `report`.

post.description: Build the published site on this machine, so a page can be looked at rather than described: the same Jekyll build `pages-publish` runs in CI, into a directory of your choosing, and never pushed. Every skill this layer can resolve, with its one-line summary. The entry point AGENTS.md sends an agent to first.

Change one existing local skill's instruction file through a gate: it must resolve as skill-fetch serves it, be tracked in the working repository, not be generated, be granted `skill-update` to the actor by a policy, be unchanged since it was read, keep its name and parse, and add only links that resolve. A gate that cannot decide refuses. Writes the working tree; the caller commits.

base_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex of the file as the caller read it.

post.description: Build a named slice of a graph (beans, todos, library, or the whole-repo kg) as one SQLite file a browser mounts without parsing it, beside a manifest carrying its sha256, a row-content digest, its row counts and the search block the one search page reads. Heavy text is indexed by a contentless FTS5 and not stored; each row points at a content-addressed payload. `--check` builds every slice twice, requires one sha256, and requires the row digest read back from the file to equal the one computed from the source.

slice.description: A slice to build; repeatable. Absent: every slice in the builder's table.

out.description: Where the files and `index.json` go; defaults to the gitignored `docs/assets/slices/`. The deploy passes `./_site/assets/slices`.

check.description: Build twice and verify instead of writing: one sha256, the row digest against the source, an FTS5 phrase query, the payload audit.

A slice over the ~5 MB budget is reported (`overBudget` in the manifest), not refused. The file's sha256 is stable for one SQLite version; `contentDigest` is the cross-version identity.

post.summary: Publish a folio's or an IG's site from the agent's own checkout — the one agent publish path
post.description: Build a repository's site in the agent's checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared `site.build` recipe (built by `build-instance-site`), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — `folio-staging.yml` for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG's `ghbuild.yml` for a FHIR IG, whose `build` job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (`sync-docs-harness`, then `rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>`): every page gains the rail and the icon row `#fa-navbar-row`, and the IG's own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose `index.html` wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; `--plan` stops there, `--dry-run` composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, `--artifact` writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead.

dryRun.description: Build and compose the commit in a temporary publish-branch worktree; push nothing.

artifact.description: Write a claude.ai Artifact bundle here instead of pushing.

workflowSource.description: An IG: read the reusable workflow from this local checkout instead of fetching it at the ref its caller names.

publisher.description: `folio` or `ig`, when the repository's workflows call both (the folio by default).

post.summary: Where to drop a file — the queue's upload URL
post.description: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer's own declaration: the `uploads` graph's directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub's `/upload/<branch>/<path>`. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared `uploads` graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no `origin` remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404.

It also answers "which queue" when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal.
x-selection.limits: It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and `upload-routes` says so rather than picking. The `/upload/<branch>/<path>` form is GitHub's, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything `upload-routes` lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout.
x-selection.cost: One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed.
